why: The statement's conjecture is the universal claim that a bounded simply connected (Lipschitz) domain failing the Pompeiu property must be a ball. One non-ball counterexample in the class refutes that claim outright, so I scored Colbrook–Stepaniants and Cao-Labora–de Dios Pont as whole and refuted, but unreviewed. Interval certificates and an authors' own Lean build are not digestion, and neither is checkable by hand. Guo v2 includes a planar convex example, so it is also scored whole. Guo events that cover only dimensions n ≥ 3 are scored case, following the record's split between the planar and higher-dimensional questions. Schiffer-only, Berenstein, spherical, discrete and homogeneous-space results are variants. Kolountzakis–Spyridakis re-proves a case known since Williams 1976, so it is none. For AI role, Guo's README says the constructions and proofs were 'produced with AI models', which is generated. Colbrook's AI use was debugging only, and the Cao-Labora AI attribution rests only on secondary sources, so both are none. I judged Ramm's 2013 and 2016 claims not_credible: they have had no uptake in over a decade, later work treats the problem as open, and they directly conflict with the 2026 counterexamples.
doubts: There are two close calls on scope. First, whether a higher-dimensional-only counterexample (Guo dim 4, dims 4/6, v1, second paper) should count as whole rather than case: if the conjecture is read as dimension-free, any one counterexample refutes it. Second, whether the statement's vague 'topology of domains' wording makes a planar counterexample only a case. For the Guo Zenodo-only events, the event-level quote says only 'assistance'; I rated them generated because the repository README that hosts this work says the proofs were AI-produced. The Pompeiu-failure proof for Guo's v2 planar example is in an unread section.
